(p-٣١٠) Surah At-Tatfif (The Defrauding)

Its purpose is to explain the end of Surah al-Infitar: that there must be a judgment of the servants on the Day of Calling, with the righteous, the people of guidance, settled in the Abode of Bliss, and the wretched, the people of misguidance and obstinacy, settled in the Blazing Fire. It indicates this by His being their Lord and the One who does good to them through the comprehensiveness of His favor. No sensible person imagines that anyone raises another without holding him accountable for what he was entrusted with and charged to do, or that He does not deal justly between those whom He nurtures. Its name, at-Tatfif, is the clearest indication of this. (In the name of Allah) Him to whom belongs perfect wisdom and complete power, (the All-Merciful) who has encompassed all by the all-inclusive favor of creation and clarification, (the Most Merciful) who has honored His party by granting them success in good dealing.

* *

When He concluded Surah al-Infitar with the cutting off of causes and the severing of lineages [on the Day of Reckoning], and emphasized the threat of the Day of Judgment and that no one has any command on that Day, (p-٣١١) and mentioned the wretched and the happy, and since the greatest thing that occurs among the servants is their fates, and since the sin of cheating in measure is among the basest and lowest sins, He warned against betrayal in it, mentioned what has been prepared for its people, and gathered to them everyone who is characterized by their description. So His forbearance described him as one of a type of sins. All of this is a warning to the heedless wretched about the deadly, sickening poisons they are in, and a pointer toward the cure for whoever wants it. [So He said]: ﴿Woe﴾, that is, a firm, great destruction in every state of the states of this world and the Hereafter, ﴿to the defrauders﴾, that is, those who diminish the measure and the balance and withhold people's rights. In this is an indication that the root of all afflictions is bad character, namely love of this world, which leads to gathering wealth from other than its lawful means, even by the basest ways: defrauding, which no person of honor accepts. They are those who come close to filling the measure and balancing the scale, yet neither fill nor balance. It may be from infaal (removal), i.e., he removes what rises above the top of the measure, from alaf, which is what rises above the land of the Arabs over the fertile lands of Iraq (rif al-'Iraq). From this is what is in the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: "I was a horseman and I outran the people until the horse leapt for me to the mosque of Bani Zurayq," meaning the horse jumped until it nearly equaled the mosque in height. It is said: "The man tatfa al-ha'it (ṭaffa al-ha'ita)," i.e., he climbed over the wall. Or it is from nearness, from their saying: "I took from my goods what was light and close (tuffa)," i.e., it came near to me. Everything that you bring close to something has been made to approach it (atfaftuhu). The tuffaf of a vessel or other thing is what comes near to filling it without completing its filling. In the hadith: "All of you are the sons of Adam, the brim of the sa'" (a measure). Or it is from taṭfīf, which is withholding, as it is said: "He tatfifa against him (ṭaffafa 'alayhi) tatfifan," meaning he stinted him. Or it is from al-ṭafīf, which is the basest, lowliest, and smallest of things. So the doubling of the letter indicates removal according to the first meaning, as has passed, and great closeness according to the second meaning, i.e., he comes very close to the full measure with deceit and trickery, until the rightful owner thinks that he has given in full while he has not given in full. It is said: "So-and-so ṭaffa to so-and-so" when he intends to deceive him. And when this is forbidden, what is less than this is forbidden even more by the implicit meaning of agreement (mafhum al-muwafaqa). On the third meaning, it means stinting and haggling over the measure. On the fourth meaning, it means diminishing and reducing in it. It seems that this word was chosen because one hardly steals in the balance and the measure except a very small amount. This is its basic meaning in the language. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has explained it, saying:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 83, verse 2:

﴿Those who, when they take measure﴾, that is, who undertake the measuring or weighing and thereby weigh (themselves) in accordance with what the following indicates. He used the particle of elevation (ʿalā, "upon") so that the meaning would be: "domineering or overbearing" ﴿over people﴾, that is, particularly in front of them, whoever they may be, [not] fearing anything and not regarding anyone, rather treachery and shamelessness have become their habit (ṭ) (p-313). This verb takes the particles min and ʿalā: one says ikhtāla min al-rajul and ʿalayhi (he took measure from the man and against him). It may be that the choice of the expression ʿalā here, together with what preceded, indicates that when they have some degree of superiority, in that the one from whom they take measure is weak, they betray him, so their affair revolves around baseness and lowness of aspiration, beyond which there is no lower state. ﴿They demand in full﴾, that is, they make for themselves the fulfilment, which is the completion of the measure, with the utmost desire and exaggeration in filling. It is as if he mentioned "ikhtālū" (when they take measure) and did not mention "ittazinū" (when they weigh) because in weighing there is not the scope for treatment that exists in measuring, and because in measuring they are able to exaggerate in demanding what leads to excess, to a degree they cannot achieve in the like of it in weighing. This is unlike cheating (ikhsār), for the capacity to do it is present in both situations, and therefore he mentioned both in it.

(p-314) When the fronting of the prepositional phrase had conveyed exclusivity, it conveyed that if they act on their own behalf, it is not the same. He made this explicit by saying: ﴿And when they measure for them or weigh for them﴾, meaning: when they measure out to people, that is, their due, that is, what is owed to them [of the right]; or when they weigh out to them, meaning they weigh out what is owed to them of the right. It is said: "ightāla min al-rajul and ʿalayhi" and "kāla lahu al-ṭaʿām" [and "kālahu al-ṭaʿām"], and "wazantu al-rajul al-shayʾ" and "wazantu lahu al-shayʾ." Perhaps He, glorified is He, chose "ʿalā" in the first and the doubly transitive form in the second because it indicates more clearly the presence of the rightful owner, whereas in his absence it is more fitting [to act deceptively], and it indicates more clearly the one who is bold in impudence. These are two words, not four, because there is no alif of plurality after the wāw. Al-Baghawi said: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar used to treat them as two separate words, pausing on kālū and wazanū and beginning with hum. Abu ʿUbayda said: the preferred view is the first. Al-Baghawi said: he means that each is one word, because they wrote them without an alif by agreement of the codices (al-maṣāḥif, the written copies of the Qur'an). Al-Zamakhshari said: it cannot be that the pronoun refers to the defrauders (al-muṭaffifīn), because the sentence would then lead to a corrupt arrangement. The meaning would be: when they take from people they demand full measure, and when they give to them they cause loss. If you make the pronoun refer to the defrauders, it becomes: "When they take from people they demand full measure, and when they themselves take charge of the measure or the weight, they cause loss." This is an incongruous statement, because the discussion concerns the act of giving, not the one directly performing it. Relying on the script of the codex, and on the claim that the alif written after the plural wāw is not original in it, to refute this is weak, because the script of the codex did not in many places follow the rules of orthography (ʿilm al-khaṭṭ) that are established for it. End of quotation. There is no doubt that the script of the codex strengthens this meaning and confirms it. ﴿They cause loss﴾, meaning they bring about loss through shortfall in what they measure for others. The summary is that they take their full measure or more, and they give less.

(p-315) Imam Abu Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr said: When the Most High, glorified is He, said in the Chapter of the Cleaving (al-Infiṭār): ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble recorders﴾ [82:10–11], and so on, the implication of that was the occurrence of recompense for the smallest details of deeds, and that no deed is lost, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We bring it forth, and sufficient are We as reckoners﴾ [21:47].

He followed the preceding verse with the recompense of a deed which one might think is committed by one close [to God in regard] to a deed, and it is among the greatest of crimes: that is defrauding in the measure and the balance and deviating from establishing justice in that. So the Most High said: ﴿Woe to the defrauders﴾ [83:1]. Then He followed their threat and the severity of their warning, saying: ﴿Do they not think that they will be resurrected﴾ [83:4], ﴿for a tremendous Day﴾ [83:5]. Then the verses were joined together, fitting with what the chapter opened with, to its end. End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 83, verse 4:

When He, glorified and exalted is He, mentioned that they had become addicted to these vices until they became a character trait to which they were accustomed, at ease with it, and content with it, and this could only come from one who felt secure from punishment and denied the reckoning, the denial of this was made to follow in the most eloquent manner, so as to convey that their condition is such that it deserves to be wondered at and questioned about, and that the one who inquires about its occurrence among them is (only) doubtful, while certainty is not conceivable regarding them, because of the remoteness of their harsh states and their rigid understandings from it. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Do not those think﴾, that is, these base, distant, impure, vile people, that at some moment there will renew for them a thought that they were not certain of the proofs that have passed, which conveyed the highest degrees of certainty. For if they thought this to any degree, it would restrain them, if they had any concern for themselves, from the likes of these ugly deeds. And whoever is not benefited by those decisive proofs with a suspicion that makes him take precautions for his own soul, has no sense at all. ﴿That they﴾, and He expressed it with the passive participle, saying: ﴿will be resurrected﴾, as an indication of the overpowering by the easiest way, through the resurrection, which they are already accustomed to in a similar form of overpowering, through waking after being overpowered by sleep.

For a great day (﴿لِيَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾). That is, for its sake and in it. He intensified the awe with His words ﴿عَظِيمٍ﴾ (great), meaning: because of the greatness of what happens on it, of the gathering and the reckoning, from which reward and punishment result, which none knows in its true reality except Him, glorified and exalted is He.

When that Day had become great as a warning against it, and He increased its greatness by following it, as a decisive statement, with His words, in the accusative by implied "I mean" (aʿnī), to inform that denial on it is before the eyes of all creation, so it is a disgrace unlike any other disgrace: ﴿The Day when mankind stands﴾, meaning on their feet, ﴿mankind﴾, meaning everyone who has the capacity for movement. That is the Day of Resurrection, fifty thousand years long, during which He, glory be to Him, does not look at them. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Kabir from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr, traced to the Prophet, and its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat). ﴿Before the Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning for the judgment of the One who originated all creatures and nurtures them all. So He forgets none of them in His provision, neglects none of them in His judgment, and does not accept the wronging of anyone He nurtures. He bestows upon each one of them from His sustenance by the judgment of nurture. All of this is from the interrogative of denunciation, and the whole of it is conjecture (al-zann). He described the Day with what He described and other than that, for emphasis in forbidding cheating in measure and magnifying its sin.

Al-Hakim narrated, through the chain of ʿAbdullah ibn Buraydah from his father, may Allah be pleased with him, traced to the Prophet: "No people break a covenant except that Allah gives their enemy power over them, and they do not rule by other than what Allah the Exalted has revealed except that poverty spreads among them, and immorality does not appear among them except that death spreads among them, and they do not cheat in measure except that they are deprived of crops and seized by years of drought, and they do not withhold zakat except that rain is withheld from them." And through the route of ʿAtaʾ ibn Abi Rabah from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr, traced to the Prophet, similar to it. And al-Tabarani has, through the route of al-Dahhak from Mujahid and Tawus from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, traced to the Prophet, similar to it.

ولَمّا أنْهى سُبْحانَهُ ما أرادَ مِن تَعْظِيمِ ذَلِكَ [اليَوْمِ - ] والتَّعْجِيبِ مِمَّنْ لَمْ يُفِدْهُ بَراهِينَهُ أنْ يُجَوِّزَهُ والإنْكارَ عَلَيْهِ، وكانَ مَعَ ما فِيهِ مِنَ التَّقْرِيعِ مُفْهِمًا لِلتَّقْرِيرِ، نَفى بِأداةِ الرَّدْعِ لِلْمُبالَغَةِ في النَّفْيِ مَضْمُونَ ما وقَعَ الِاسْتِفْهامُ عَنْهُ فَقالَ: ﴿كَلا﴾ أيْ لا يَظُنُّ أُولَئِكَ ذَلِكَ بِوَجْهٍ مِنَ الوُجُوهِ لِكَثافَةِ طِباعِهِمْ ووُقُوفِهِمْ مَعَ المَحْسُوسِ دَأبَ البَهائِمُ بَلْ لا يُجَوِّزُونَهُ، ولَوْ جَوَّزُوهُ لَما وقَعُوا في ظُلْمِ أحَدٍ مَن يَسْألُونَ عَنْهُ في ذَلِكَ اليَوْمِ المَهُولِ، وما أوْجَبَ لَهُمُ الوُقُوعَ في الجَرائِمِ إلّا الإعْراضُ عَنْهُ، وقالَ (p-٣١٨)الحَسَنُ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعالى: هي بِمَعْنى حَقًّا مُتَّصِلَةً بِما بَعْدَها - انْتَهى. وهي مَعَ ذَلِكَ مُفْهِمَةٌ لِلرَّدْعِ الَّذِي لَيْسَ بَعْدَهُ رَدْعٌ عَنِ اعْتِقادِ مِثْلِ ذَلِكَ والمُوافَقَةِ لِشَيْءٍ مِمّا يُوجِبُ الخِزْيَ فِيهِ.

ولَمّا أخْبَرَ عَنْ إنْكارِهِمُ، اسْتَأْنَفَ إثْباتَ ما أنْكَرُوهُ عَلى أبْلَغِ وجْهٍ وأفْظَعِهِ مُهَوِّلًا لِما يَقَعُ لَهم مِنَ الشُّرُورِ وفَواتِ السُّرُورِ، مُؤَكِّدًا لِأجْلِ إنْكارِهِمْ فَقالَ: ﴿إنَّ كِتابَ﴾ وأظْهَرَ مَوْضِعَ الإضْمارِ تَعْمِيمًا وتَعْلِيقًا لِلْحُكْمِ بِالوَصْفِ فَقالَ: ﴿الفُجّارِ﴾ أيْ صَحِيفَةَ حِسابِ هَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ حَمَلَهم عَلى كُفْرِهِمْ مُرُوقِهِمْ وكَذا كُلُّ مَن وافَقَهم في صِفاتِهِمْ فَكانَ في غايَةِ المُرُوقِ مِمّا حَقَّ مُلابَسَتَهُ ومُلازَمَتَهُ، وأبْلَغَ في التَّأْكِيدِ فَقالَ: ﴿لَفِي سِجِّينٍ﴾ هو عِلْمٌ مَنقُولٌ في صِيغَةِ المُبالَغَةِ عَنْ وصْفِ [مِنَ - ] السِّجْنِ وهو الحَبْسُ لِأنَّهُ سَبَبُ الحَبْسِ في جَهَنَّمَ أيْ إنَّهُ لَيْسَ فِيهِ أهْلِيَّةِ الصُّعُودِ إلى مَحَلِّ الأقْداسِ إشارَةٌ إلى أنَّ كِتابَهم إذا كانَ في سِجْنٍ عَظِيمٍ أيْ ضَيِّقٍ شَدِيدٍ كانُوا هم [فِي - ] أعْظَمَ، قالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: وهي (p-٣١٩)الأرْضُ السّابِعَةُ - انْتَهى [وهُوَ يَفْهَمُ -] مَعَ هَذِهِ الحَقِيقَةِ أنَّهم في غايَةِ الخَسارَةِ لِأنَّهُ يُقالُ لِكُلِّ مَنِ انْحَطَّ: صارَ تُرابًا ولَصِقَ بِالأرْضِ - ونَحْوُ ذَلِكَ،

Then he increased its terror by informing that it is deserving of being asked about and of being struck (as a proverb) to the world, (even if it could be reached) by the armpits of camels. So He said: ﴿And what will make you know what Sijjin is?﴾ That is, He made you one who knows, even if you strive for that. ﴿What is Sijjin?﴾ That is, it is of such a nature that minds cannot comprehend its description. And it, along with that, is in the lowest of the low, and it is witnessed by the distant ones among the devils and the rest of the wrongdoers. It ascends with the dead person [from among them] to the sky, and its gates are closed against him, so he returns, and the wind hurls him down, and the devils rejoice over him.

And everything in which He said "And what will make you know" (wa-ma adraka), He then did make him know of it; this is unlike "And what will make you know" (wa-ma yudrika), which is used differently.

When he had completed what he intended of its description, he turned away from elaborating on it, as a sign that it is of such greatness that description falls short of it. He then resumed the matter of the Book in which it is confined, saying, warning against it and magnifying its affair: ﴿A Book﴾, that is, great in preserving the smallest and the tiniest [of deeds], ﴿inscribed﴾, that is, written out clearly, as the white mark is distinct on the black hide of a bull. Everyone who sees it knows that it is the utmost in evil. It is like the inscription in cloth and the engraving in stone, which neither wears away nor is effaced.

Now that he has made known the evil that awaits the record of the wicked, he resumes the report of what it produces for its companions, saying: ﴿Woe﴾, meaning the greatest destruction, ﴿on that day﴾, meaning the day when people stand before what has been mentioned. Since the original wording would have been "for them," he replaced it with an apparent description, to generalize and to make the judgment depend on it, saying: ﴿to the deniers﴾, meaning those firmly rooted in denial of everything that ought to be affirmed.

al-Biqa'i said: When He had told of their woe, He described them with what makes clear what they denied, and what goes further in blaming them. So He said: ﴿Those who deny﴾, meaning they consistently deny everyone whose word ought to be believed, scorning ﴿the Day of﴾, meaning on account of the report of the Day of ﴿the Recompense﴾, that is, the judgment, which is the secret of existence.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 83, verse 12:

﴿Wa-ma﴾ i.e., while the situation is that he does not ﴿deny﴾, i.e., does not commit denial ﴿of it except every transgressor﴾, i.e., one who exceeds the limit in obstinacy or in dullness and blind imitation (taqlid), because the point at which one attributes to someone who has been established by conclusive proofs that He is capable of everything, to being incapable of repeating what He originated, ﴿sinful﴿, i.e., one who goes to extremes in indulging in desires that necessitate sins, which are the wrongdoings, so that his heart is blackened and he becomes blind, by the sight of desires that are surrounded by the Fire, to everything other than them.

When he had established for him the act of conveying sin, He indicated it by his saying, with the particle of certainty: ﴿When Our verses are recited﴾, i.e., by whatever reciter it may be, [the verses] being elevated by the proofs they possess ﴿upon him﴾, i.e., the signs indicating what is intended to be made clear to him, together with [what] they have of greatness in relation to Us. ﴿He says﴾, i.e., without pausing or reflecting, but rather out of self-interest, which led him into the desire to dominate, the cause of which is arrogance: ﴿Tales of the ancients﴾, i.e., of falsehoods, and they are not the words of Allah. Thus, because of the extreme extent of his ignorance, he does not benefit from the evidences of transmission, just as he has not considered the proofs of reason.

Since this person has become like the cattle in failing to reflect, and is indeed further astray in the way, because he is able to reflect and they are not, He says, rebuking him, refuting him, and explaining what led him to this statement, though he does not truly hold it: ﴿Nay!﴾ That is, let him be deterred with a great deterrence and restrained with a strong restraint. The matter is not as he said in the recited words, nor does he hold it as a firm belief, because he did not say it from insight. ﴿Rather, what they used to earn has covered﴾, that is, overpowered, enveloped, and concealed, as clouds cover the sky and rust covers a mirror. He used the plural (ʿalā qulūbihim, "over their hearts") in consideration of the meaning of "kull" (every), so that no one seeking to find fault could object. He then spoke with the plural of multitude, indicating their great number: ﴿over their hearts﴾, that is, every one who uttered this statement. ﴿What they used to earn﴾, that is, by their corrupt natural dispositions, ﴿they used to earn﴾, that is, they renewed their earning of it, persisting in it, through evil deeds. For the multiplication of acts is a cause for the acquisition of firm dispositions (malakāt, "settled character traits"): if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. Thus sin accumulates upon the heart and it becomes black. For this reason they used to say this kind of belief. Indeed, it is something by which they close the assembly, make excuses for themselves before the common people, and weaken the resolve of the reciters, with what they burn of their hearts (may Allah burn their hearts and their houses with fire). For they do not cease in any age, nor do they fear shame or disgrace. (p-322) Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī, and Ibn Mājah related from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "When the servant commits a sin, a black spot is marked on his heart. If he repents, it is polished away; if he increases (in sin), it increases until it covers his heart. That is the rān (covering) of which Allah, glorified and exalted, spoke."

Al-Ghazālī said in the Kitāb al-Tawba of the Iḥyāʾ: It has already been mentioned that a person, at the beginning of his creation, is not free from following desires, and every desire a person follows raises a darkness to his heart, just as darkness rises from the self of a person to the face of a mirror [the polished one. If the darkness of desires accumulates, it becomes rayn, as the vapor of the self becomes on the face of a mirror -] when it accumulates as filth. When the rayn accumulates, it becomes a nature like the filth on the face of a mirror when it accumulates and its time lengthens. It penetrates the body of the iron and corrupts it, and it no longer accepts polishing afterward, and becomes like something imprinted by filth. Abandoning the following of desires in the future is not sufficient to remedy them; rather, it is necessary to erase those traces that have been imprinted on the heart, just as ceasing the breaths and dark vapors that darken the mirror's face in the future is not sufficient for the image to appear in the mirror unless one works at erasing what has been imprinted on it of traces. And just as darkness of sins and desires rises to the heart, light from acts of obedience and abandoning desires rises to it, so the darkness of disobedience is erased by the light of obedience. To this is the allusion in his (ﷺ) saying: "Follow the evil deed with a good deed, and it will wipe it out."

(p-323) Since their claim was merely a statement uttered with their mouths, which does not go beyond them at all, He repeated His deterrence of them from it and His denial of it, saying: ﴿Nay!﴾ That is, the matter is not as they said, these fables, neither in reality nor in their own view; so let them desist from it with the utmost desistance. And since a person's saying what he does not believe and what is not actually so is, as is most astonishing, hardly credible, He gave the reason, explaining that what drives them to it is only the veil with which Allah, glorified is He, sealed their hearts. So He said, emphasizing it for those among the deluded who deny this: ﴿Indeed they, from their Lord﴾, that is, from the remembrance of the One who does good to them, and fear of Him, and hope in Him, ﴿on that Day﴾, that is, when they uttered this empty saying, ﴿will be veiled.﴾ Since the barrier is only the veil, the verb is put in the passive form, ﴿mahjubun (veiled)﴾. Therefore the devils and the vain desires gained dominion over them, and they came to say what, had the beasts possessed reason, they would have been ashamed to say. The better view is that the verse is an explanation and a justification of their woe which was mentioned earlier, the sense being: "on the day when it is the Day of Judgment," and the intended meaning is the veiling from seeing Him, and in this there is good news for the believers of it. Al-Baghawi said: Most of the commentators said: "from seeing Him." He also said: The two Imams, al-Shafi'i and his teacher Malik, took this verse as evidence for the vision (of Allah). The memorizer Abu Nu'aym, in al-Hilya, in the biography of al-Shafi'i, related that he said: "In this verse is an indication that His friends will see Him in His attributes." Ibn al-Fadl said: Just as He veiled them in this world from His Oneness, so He veils them in the Hereafter from seeing Him. Al-Hasan said: "If the ascetics and the worshippers knew that they would not see their Lord in the return, their souls would have expired in this world." Al-Qushayri said: The implication of the address requires that the believers will see Him as they know Him today [end of quote]. And in it is an analogy: their humiliation is likened to the humiliation of one who prevents entry into the presence of a king.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 83, verse 16:

When he had explained what punishment awaits them through being veiled, which is the punishment of the heart, the punishment than which there is none more severe, because all punishment branches out from it, he began to explain some of what branches out from it of the punishment of the body, emphasizing it because of their denial, and expressing it with the particle of delay (thumma) to indicate the high rank of this punishment among the kinds of punishment. So He said: ﴿Then indeed they will be burning in the Hellfire﴾, meaning: after what Allah wills of their being given respite, ﴿they will be burning in the Hellfire﴾, meaning they will enter the great Fire and remain therein, suffering its heat and being immersed in it as a roasted sheep is immersed, that is, the roasted one.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 83, verse 17:

When He had explained what befalls them of the action that pertains to the heart and to the body, He followed it with speech of reproach and rebuke, which is the torment of the soul. He made the verb passive (yuqal) because what causes the rebuke is hearing it, not who utters it from a specific speaker, and to indicate that every being capable of speech may address them with it, whether the keepers of the Fire, the people of Paradise, or others, since they have no defense. ﴿Then it will be said﴾, that is, to them, after a period, as rebuke, reproach, censure and denunciation: ﴿This﴾, that is, the torment that now befalls you, ﴿is what you used to deny﴾ (p. 325), that is, by reason of the wicked dispositions that you possessed, ﴿in it﴾, that is, specifically, because your denial of other things is in comparison to it, due to its ugliness and to your firm entrenchment in it and constant adherence to it (?), ﴿you used to deny﴾, that is, you kept bringing about denial of it, renewing it, persisting in it.

Since this might suggest that they see all of their punishment at that time, He negated that with His saying: ﴿Nay﴾, meaning: it is not the whole, but a single instance of the kind. Therefore the kind acted upon it, and it is their *nuzul* (the prepared provision or welcome). The matter is too vast and too great for description to encompass. Having mentioned the punishment of the deniers, which their attachment to this world brought upon them, and beginning with it because the context from the start of the surah is one of warning and piercing threats, He followed it with what belongs to the affirmers, whom He draws toward happiness: abandoning their portions and turning away from the hastened desires of this world. So He said, emphasizing it against their denial: ﴿Indeed, the record of the righteous﴾, meaning the scroll of the good deeds of those who are at the furthest extent in the expansion of their breasts, the breadth of their intellects, the abundance and purity of their deeds, and other excellent qualities of theirs, ﴿is in ʿIlliyyūn﴾, meaning places attributed to highness. The attribution came first to a singular form, *fiʿlī* (the nisba, or relative adjective, formed from a noun), and then it was made plural, [although -] it has no singular from its own form, like *ʿishrūn* (twenty) and its counterparts. Al-Kisāʾī said: When the Arabs pluralize what they do not regard as having a base from one or two, they pluralize it with the *wāw* and *nūn* for the masculine and feminine, and that is the end of his statement. So they are ascending degrees that rise up to God and are not veiled from Him, unlike the wicked, whose degrees are some above [others -] without end, according to the ranks of deeds. And everyone whose record is among the righteous will join the place of it, just as everyone whose record is among the wicked will join Sijjīn. Al-Rāzī said in *al-Lawāmiʿ*: Whoever's knowledge ascends above the senses and imaginings, and whose action is beyond the dictates of desire and anger, is worthy of being exalted. Whoever's knowledge and perception are confined to the senses, imagination and fancies, and whose action follows the dictates of bestial appetites, is worthy of being in Sijjīn.

When this was a matter of great magnitude, he increased its magnification by His saying: ﴿And what will make you know what ʿIlliyyun is?﴾ That is, what thing will make you aware, meaning, what will make you a knower of it, even if you exert yourself greatly in investigation? For its description is something the intellects cannot contain, and its loftiness necessarily entails an absolute expanse and a manifest vastness.

Now, when he had magnified the place, so that the greatness of the Book became known, he began the report about it in an assertive manner, to increase its greatness, and said: ﴿A Book﴾, meaning a great one, ﴿inscribed﴾, meaning that in it [that] so-and-so is safe from the Fire. How wondrous is that inscription, how beautiful, how splendid, and how lovely!

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 83, verse 21:

When He magnified it in its own essence and in its station, He magnified it in its presence (ḥiḍār), saying: ﴿Witnessed by those brought near﴾. That is, it is attended by them with complete and continuous presence, with no absence in it: the group (al-jamā'ah) (p-327) who everyone knows have no nearness to any who considers their nearness except nearness from its beginning to its end. They are the witnesses of this inscribed record, and they are the angels, who escort it from heaven to heaven and surround it with joy and with honor for its owner. And those in the heavens witness it too, from among the prophets, peace be upon them, and the truthful (ṣiddīqīn), the martyrs, and the righteous. So this verse, together with the first, is an instance of iḥtibāk (interlocking elision): the mention of Sijjīn first indicates the lowest rank, and the mention of ʿIlliyyīn and "those brought near" second indicates the lowest of the low and "those removed" first.

Now that their record has been magnified with these excellences, the discourse turned to describing their state, and He said, healing the ignorance of this shift and emphasizing for the sake of the one who denies: ﴿Indeed, the righteous﴾, that is, those whose record is this, ﴿are surely in bliss﴾, that is, encompassing them, the opposite of what the wicked have of the blazing fire:

Since nothing is more pleasurable for a person than a high place on which to sit and to cast his gaze upon whatever he desires among what is before him, He said, explaining that delight: ﴿Upon couches﴾, that is, on high beds, [together with this] absolute elevation in the canopies, whose description baffles thought because of their loftiness, adorned with pearls and rubies and other things that cannot be enumerated. ﴿They gaze﴾, that is, upon what they desire of the gardens, the rivers, the maidens of paradise (hur) and the youths (wildan). They have no occupation other than that, and whatever resembles it of delights. Imam al-Qushayri said: He affirmed the gazing but did not specify what is gazed upon, because of their differing: among them are those who gaze upon their palaces, and among them are those who gaze upon their maidens, and among them... and among them... (p-328). The elite (al-khawass), at all times, gaze toward God Most High, just as the wicked are perpetually veiled from their Lord.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 83, verse 24:

When He had described their bliss, He informed that, because of their deep-rootedness in it, every observer who looks at them recognizes them by it. So He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿You will recognize﴾, that is, O observer of them, this being according to the reading of the majority. Abu Ja'far and Ya'qub read it in the passive voice, which is more indicative of generality, ﴿in their faces﴾ when they are seen, ﴿the radiance of bliss﴾, that is, its brightness, its splendour, its beauty, its sheen and its freshness, from "nadara" (to be radiant), said of a plant when it blossoms and flowers. Al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "The radiance (nadra) is in the face, and the joy (surur) is in the heart."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 83, verse 25:

Since gatherings of delight, especially in verdant places, are not pleasant without food and drink, and since drink implies eating, he (Allah) mentioned only the drink, because these surahs are short and He intends to gather meanings together with brevity. He said: ﴿They will be given to drink﴾, constructing the verb in the passive voice (bani lahu lil-maf'ul) to indicate that they are always served, with no burden upon them in anything. ﴿From a sealed wine﴾, that is, a pure, clear, unadulterated, white, fragrant drink of the utmost delight. They said: the rahiq (rahiq, a pure wine) is wine, or the best of it, or its finest, or the pure, or the clear, and a kind of fragrance. There is no doubt that a sensible person does not drink wine at all, so how much less its finest, unless he has completed its prerequisites of food, drink, clothing, marriage and other things. Since sealing is only for what has great rank and whose preciousness is rare, he said, intending either the literal meaning or a metaphor for its preciousness: ﴿sealed﴾, that is, it is, with its preciousness, free from dust and all impurities and filth.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 83, verse 26:

Since the sealing (al-khatm) at the moment of unsealing must necessarily leave a residue from its dregs in the drink, he said: ﴿Its seal is musk﴾. Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: the intended meaning of "its seal" is the last of its taste. The result is that its seal, at the beginning of its opening and at the end of its drinking, is musk. This requires that no one opens it except its drinker, and that it will be in proportion to his sufficiency, so he drinks all of it. The expression is suitable for the seal to be both first and last, and this runs in the manner of the deflowering of a virgin.

Since the implied sense is: "In it the drinkers reach the extreme of pleasure," he followed it with his saying: ﴿And in that﴾, i.e., in the great matter, far-reaching in its attainment, which is the life of delight and bliss and the drink of which this is the description, ﴿let those who strive for it strive﴾, i.e., let them desire it with the utmost desire, with all effort and choice. ﴿Those who strive﴾, i.e., those for whom rivalry (al-munafasah) is characteristic, which is that each of them seeks that this thing contested for be for himself alone, to the exclusion of others, because it is very precious (nafis). The precious (al-nafis) is that for which people's souls are eager and which they prize highly. And rivalry in such a thing is through abundance of righteous deeds and sincere intentions.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 83, verse 27:

When he mentioned the drink, he followed it with its mixture, in accordance with what the people of this world are accustomed to, but with something more noble than it. So he said, clarifying the state of this one who is given to drink: ﴿And its mixture﴾, meaning: they are given to drink from it, while the mixture of this sealed nectar is ﴿from Tasnim﴾, which is a proper name for a specific spring. Being a proper name, it also indicates that this spring is lofty in place and rank. The drink is poured down upon them from its water [from above], and Hamzah al-Karmani said: its water flows over the air, scented, and pours into the vessels of the people of Paradise according to the measure of need; when they are full, it stops. In poetry, Tasnim is the name of a high mountain, and likewise Tan'im. Its root is from sanam (hump), and for this reason he (the commentator) cut it off, praising it, saying:

"A spring from which the ones brought near will drink" — i.e., by means of it, in the manner of a mixture from it. ﴿Al-muqarrabun﴾ means those whose being brought near has occurred through the drawing of the Truth toward them, and the restriction of their aspirations to it. Every drink they desire [is theirs]. As for the righteous (al-abrar), they drink from it only the rahiq (the pure wine). As for others, they do not reach it at all. Some of them said: the ones brought near drink from this spring pure, unmixed, while the righteous are given it mixed, and the difference is evident — wholesome for them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 83, verse 29:

When He, glorified is He, mentioned the recompense of the disbeliever with the Blazing Fire (al-Jahim) and the recompense of the believer with bliss (al-na'im), (p-331) and since among the things that complete bliss is gloating over the enemy, He gave the reason for the recompense of the disbeliever by that which contains the gloating of the believer over him, because he occupied himself in this world with what does not benefit him, and so it followed that he forfeited what would benefit him. Then He said, emphasizing it, because people of honor, lofty resolve, sound disposition and upright temperament can hardly believe the like of this, and He emphasized it to indicate that it is his right not to be [such a person]: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes﴾, that is, those who severed what Allah commanded to be joined, ﴿used to﴾, that is, in the world, as a habit, a character, a nature and an innate disposition, ﴿laugh at those who believed﴾, that is, even if they were at the lowest ranks of faith, ﴿they would renew their laughter whenever they saw them, or they would remind one another of them, mocking them and their circumstances, in which they were marked by the signs of faith: in the shabbiness of their conditions, the scarcity of their wealth, [and] the contempt of people for them, together with their claim that Allah, exalted is He, will surely help them and raise their cause.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 83, verse 30:

﴿And when they passed by them﴾, i.e., those who believed, ﴿by them﴾, i.e., by those who committed crimes, at any time whatsoever, they would mock, ﴿and they would wink at one another﴾, i.e., some of those who committed crimes would wink at one another in order to harm those who believed.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 83, verse 31:

When He had described them in places of hesitation and fluctuation, He described them in their dwellings, saying: ﴿And when they returned﴾, i.e., those who committed crimes returned, eager to return and turning to it without reluctance, ﴿to their families﴾, i.e., their dwellings which were populated (p-332) with their companions, ﴿they returned﴾ while they were ﴿jesting﴾, i.e., taking extreme delight in what they had of power and eminence, which brought them to mock others. He (Ibn Burjan) said: The Prophet (ﷺ) also mentioned: "Islam began as something strange and will return to being strange as it began. Holding on to its religion will be like holding a burning coal." And in another narration: "The believer among them will be more humiliated than a flock (ummah)." And in another: "The scholar among them will be fouler than the carcass of a donkey." So God is the One sought for help.

When he mentioned their passing by them, he mentioned the general fact of their seeing them, so he said: ﴿And when they saw them﴾, that is, when those who committed crimes saw those who believed, ﴿they said﴾, that is, upon seeing the believers, emphatically, because they sense that every person of intellect would deny them, pointing to belittling them with a demonstrative of nearness: ﴿Indeed, these are surely astray﴾, that is, those who believed are deeply immersed in error, because they abandoned this world for something greater that has no soundness.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 83, verse 33:

﴿Wa-mā﴾ — that is, and the situation is that they [— ma-] ﴿were not sent﴾, that is, no sent one (mursal) at all ﴿over them﴾, that is, over those who believed specifically, so that this solicitude on their part for them, within their homes and outside them when they pass by them and otherwise, would be warranted ﴿as guardians﴾, that is, diligently keeping watch over the deeds of those who believed. So what is their preoccupation with them to such an extent, if they are, in their estimation, among the fallen and neglected? And what is this meticulous attentiveness to their conditions, if they are among those looked upon and cared for? Let them then demonstrate the corruption of their state by a means that reason accepts and that is supported by evidence (p-333), or let them follow them. Otherwise they are not acquainted with the places of reform and with handling matters in their proper manner. How deserving they are of the words of the poet:

"Sa'd brought it to water, while Sa'd was (still) being fed; / this is not how camels are brought to water, O Sa'd."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 83, verse 34:

Since there is no bliss greater than gloating over an enemy, especially when it is at the highest levels of gloating, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So today﴾, that is, as a consequence of their deeds in the abode of action, it will be in the abode of recompense ﴿those who believed﴾, even if they were at the lowest ranks of faith, ﴿[will laugh] at the disbelievers﴾ specifically, namely those who were firmly rooted in disbelief from among the general category of those who committed crimes, in the gathering place and in Paradise, mockingly and scornfully. For those who believed do not laugh at the sinful believers even if they see them being punished; rather, they have mercy on them because they share the same religion. ﴿They will laugh﴾ as retribution and recompense, when they see the humiliation they are in, joyfully at their state, thankful to Allah for what He has given them of salvation from the Fire and of vengeance upon their enemies. Abu Salih said: The doors are opened for them, and it is said to them, "Come out," so they hasten, but when they reach the doors, they are shut in their faces, and they are returned in the most wretched state; so the believers laugh. End of quotation. And what a disgrace, and shame, and blackening of faces, and anguish of heart, and self-reproach, from the torment of the Fire, and from being mocked and disgraced! (p-334) While those who believed are kings.

On the couches (al-arā'ik), i.e., the elevated, adorned couches which, by their beauty, are fit to bear the one reclining upon them. ﴿They will gaze﴾, i.e., they will renew their staring glances at them whenever they wish, and they will see what they are in of humiliation, abasement and punishment after honor and bliss, a gaze of one seeking information (nazar al-mustafhim).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 83, verse 36:

﴿Hal thuwwiba﴾ [Has been rewarded]: He (God) built it in the passive voice because the object of the recompense is the verb itself, the rewarding in general. ﴿al-kuffar﴾ [the disbelievers]: that is, the rewarding of the two groups in disbelief occurred, meaning that they were given reward and recompense in the fullest measure. Accordingly, the clause is in the place of an accusative after ﴿yanzurun﴾ [they look]. ﴿Ma kanu﴾ [what they used to]: that is, the very act of theirs, with what is natural to them, as innate dispositions ﴿yafʿalun﴾ [do], [that is -] by their corrupt motives and their blameworthy desires. So the clause is in the place of the object. It is known that they have the woe with which the surah opened, by way of threat against one who does the deed of someone who does not believe he will be recompensed for his action. Its end concerns those who diminish people's honour in secret, [and -] its beginning concerns those who diminish wealth in the same way, and the rejection of justice and fidelity. God is the Guide to what is right, and to Him is the return and the homecoming, and to Him is the repentance.
